p: death than the day of one's: He speaks thus after the judgment of the flesh, which thinks death is the end of all evils, or else because this corporal death is the entering into everlasting life.
mourning: Where we may see the hand of God and learn to examine our lives.
thorns under a pot: Which crackle for a while and profit nothing.
mad: A man that is esteemed wise, when he falls to oppression, becomes like a beast.
end of a thing than its: He notes their lightness who attempt a thing and suddenly leave it off again.
wisely concerning this: Murmur not against God when he sends adversities for man's sins.
inheritance: He answers to them who do not value wisdom unless riches are joined with it, showing that both are the gifts of God, but that wisdom is far more excellent and may be without riches.
consider: Consider why God sends it and what may comfort you.
nothing after him: That man should be able to control nothing in his works.
righteousness: Meaning that cruel tyrants put the godly to death and let the wicked go free.
over much: Do not boast too much of your own justice and wisdom.
over much wicked: Do not tarry long when you are admonished to come out of the way of wickedness.
this: That is, on these admonitions that go before.
this withdraw not thy hand: Consider what desolation and destruction will come, if you do not obey them.
heed to all words that are: Credit them not, neither care for them.
find out the account: That is, to come to a conclusion.
devices: And so are cause for their own destruction.
